name: What's the difference between sewer line locating and a sewer camera inspection?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between sewer line locating and a sewer camera inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sewer line locating focuses on identifying the exact underground path and depth of your sewer pipes. It uses a transmitter and receiver to map the physical layout. A sewer camera inspection, on the other hand, involves inserting a waterproof camera into the pipe to visually assess its internal condition, identifying issues like cracks, blockages, root intrusion, or corrosion. Often, these services are performed together: the camera identifies internal problems, and the integrated locating feature then precisely maps where those problems are located underground. This combination offers a comprehensive understanding of your sewer system.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sewer line locating maps the pipe's underground path, while a camera inspection visually assesses its internal condition. They are often combined for comprehensive analysis.
